podcast.body: Originally intended for Bowie's *Ziggy Stardust* album, this song was instead offered to Mott the Hoople when Bowie learned they were breaking up, after they rejected his initial offer of "Suffragette City." It became Mott the Hoople's signature song. The track explores themes of electricity loss and kids no longer wanting rock music, with Ziggy delivering "no news" to them. Despite lines like "Lucy looks sweet because he dresses like a queen," often interpreted as a gay anthem, Bowie denied this intention, but acknowledged that art is open to interpretation. Written and produced by Bowie, it became a Top 40 hit in the United States in November 1972, reached number three in the UK, and was recognized by the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004 as one of the "500 songs that shaped Rock and Roll." "All the young dudes was written and produced by David Bowie."

podcast.body: Written by David Bowie, this song was performed by Mott the Hoople and served as inspiration for Noel Gallagher when composing Oasis' "Don't Look Back In Anger." "His inspiration was the Bowie written, Moth the Hoopal performed hit, all the young dudes from 1972."
